chapter: Life and its Diversity: Levels of Organisation
trick: Climb the ladder in one direction only: cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism. Every level is made of the one below it, so if you can say what a thing is made of, you know where it sits.

video.query: levels of biological organisation cell tissue organ system class 9 biology

data.prompt: Arrange the levels of organisation from the simplest upwards.

items.label: Cell
items.note: The smallest unit that can be called living

items.label: Tissue
items.note: A group of similar cells doing one job, such as muscle tissue

items.label: Organ
items.note: Several tissues working together, such as the heart

items.label: Organ system
items.note: Organs working together, such as the circulatory system

items.label: Organism
items.note: All the systems together, making one living individual

chapter: Physiological Processes: Photosynthesis, Respiration and Transpiration
trick: Photosynthesis and respiration are the same equation read backwards. One takes in carbon dioxide and water and stores energy in glucose; the other burns glucose and gives the carbon dioxide and water back. Write one and you can write the other by reversing the arrow.

video.query: photosynthesis respiration transpiration difference class 9 life science

data.prompt: Which process does each statement describe?

items.label: Carbon dioxide is taken in and oxygen given out
Oxygen is taken in and carbon dioxide given out
Happens only in the presence of light
Goes on day and night in every living cell
Water vapour escapes through the stomata
Creates the pull that draws water up the stem

trick: Animals have an organ for waste; plants simply store it or throw it away with a leaf. Among animals the excretory product tells you where the creature lives: plenty of water means ammonia, land means urea or uric acid, because saving water costs the animal energy.

video.query: excretion in plants and animals ammonotelic ureotelic uricotelic class 9

data.prompt: Match each organism or plant part with the waste it gets rid of.

trick: Name the pathogen group before you name the cure. Antibiotics work on bacteria and do nothing at all to a virus, which is why a doctor will not give them for a common cold. If the question mentions a vaccine, it is about prevention, not treatment.

video.query: communicable diseases pathogens immunity vaccination class 9 life science

data.prompt: Match each disease with the kind of organism that causes it.

trick: Energy in a food chain only ever moves one way and mostly gets lost. About a tenth passes to the next level, which is why chains are short and why there are always far more plants than tigers.

video.query: ecosystem food chain trophic levels energy flow class 9 life science

data.prompt: Complete the account of an ecosystem. Two words in the bank are decoys.
data.text: Green plants make their own food and are therefore called {1}. Animals that eat them are {2} consumers, and the animals that eat those are {3} consumers. Bacteria and fungi break dead matter down and are called {4}. Each feeding level is known as a {5} level, and only about {6} per cent of the energy passes from one to the next.
